questions.q: What does the summary say you should base your decisions on?
a: Human behavior, which stays stable over time
Forecasts about specific future events
Economic statistics from the last decade
Trends that appear in the news each day
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues the world is unpredictable but people keep responding to fear, greed and opportunity in the same ways.

questions.q: What point does Buffett's Snickers story make?
a: Some things change while others never do
Candy bars are a risky investment
Advertising drives all consumer habits
Recessions destroy brand loyalty
questions.why: The overview uses the same best-selling candy bar across decades to show that some things stay constant.

questions.q: According to the summary, what moves markets more than statistics?
a: Stories that people find compelling
Interest rate announcements
Quarterly earnings reports
Government regulations
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a good narrative beats the best data, and humans prefer tales over tells.

questions.q: What does the summary say about learning from other people's experience?
a: Some lessons only sink in once you live them yourself
Reading about mistakes is enough to avoid them
Advice from friends replaces firsthand experience
Every generation learns from the one before it
questions.why: Lesson 3 says certain things cannot be understood until you feel them, no matter how much you read or hear.

questions.q: Which experiences does Housel say have to be firsthand?
a: Big success and losing a large part of your money
Buying your first home and changing jobs
Raising children and traveling abroad
Starting a business and hiring staff
questions.why: Lesson 3 names outsized success and a loss of 30 percent or more as things you must experience to understand.
